//: WAR: THE FRONT, THE HOME FRONT, THE SACK AND THE PEACE (docs/events/war.md). Threads: out_of_the_line or ran_from_the_battle marks an officer officer_owed or officer_wronged, read at the next our_peace by a_laurel_at_the_peace or the_other_dispatch; a_place_in_the_fleet marks a young relative at_the_front (or kept_from_war), read by blooded_in_battle; taken_in_battle may mark a prisoner on_parole, read by the_parole_broken; the_spoils_of_a_sack may mark the sacker war_partner, read by a_scandal_in_the_accounts when a war with a nation is next over (nation_war_over). Core marks (FleetSystem): in_the_battle, taken_prisoner, held_to_the_peace, on_parole, bears_down_on_us and enemy_bears_down, our_peace; (NationSystem) sacked_beyond, nation_war_over.

effects.text: {self.name} wrote {officer.name}'s name into the dispatch of the victory, and what {officer.name} had done. {officer.name} read it twice.
{self.name} had a word in the Admiralty's ear, and {officer.name} went up a step for the day {officer.name} broke the line.
{self.name} had {officer.name} told, in front of the wardroom, that a battle won against orders is a battle won by luck. The wardroom approved. {officer.name} did not.
The dispatch of the victory said the turn of the flank was {self.name}'s plan. {officer.name}, who had been there, knew better, and said nothing yet.
{self.name} took the command from {officer.name} on the quarterdeck, in front of the crews. The Reach heard that the house does not keep officers who run. The wardroom heard something else.
{self.name}'s report of the defeat put the break in the line somewhere {officer.name} had not been. {officer.name} knows what it cost to write.
{self.name} asked {officer.name} why, and was told: the signal was wrong, and staying would have lost every ship. {self.name} went over the plots that night and found it was true.
{self.name} put {officer.name}'s name to the Senate at the peace, and the Senate honoured it. {officer.name} swore to {self.name} that day, in the old form, and meant it.
At the peace {self.name} gave {officer.name} a purse from the house for the war. It was well spent, and {officer.name} said so.
{self.name} thanked {officer.name} for the war, warmly, and left it there.
{self.name} answered {officer.name}'s account in the Senate, point by point, and the chamber believed {self.name}. {officer.name} will not forget the day either.
{self.name} went to {officer.name} and said that the account was fair. It was said in private, and repeated everywhere.
{officer.name}'s account stopped being copied. Four hundred credits of the house's had gone to {officer.name}, and both of them knew why.
{self.name} said nothing about {officer.name}'s account. People drew their own conclusions.
{self.name} found {kin.name} a berth in the house's fleet, and watched the shuttle go up.
{self.name} took {kin.name} onto the staff, where they could be watched, and taught.
{self.name} found {kin.name} a post at the yards: war work, the fleet's work, and nowhere near the guns. {kin.name} knew exactly what it was.
{self.name} said no. {kin.name} did not argue, which was worse.
{kin.name} came out of the first battle a step higher in the service. {self.name} had asked, and the Admiralty had agreed that it was earned.
{self.name} brought {kin.name} home after the first battle. {kin.name} came, and has not forgiven it.
{self.name} wrote back and left {kin.name} where they were. They stayed with the fleet, and grew harder.
{prisoner.house} paid four hundred credits for {prisoner.name}, and {prisoner.name} went home in a hired shuttle.
{prisoner.name} went home to {prisoner.house} in exchange for two companies of the house's crews, taken in an earlier fight.
{self.name} let {prisoner.name} go home on their word not to bear arms against {self.house} again while this war lasts.
{prisoner.name} of {prisoner.house} walked through the capital behind {self.name}'s colours, in chains, and will be held until the peace.
{self.name} told the Senate what {parolee.name}'s word was worth, and what {parolee.house}'s was. The chamber took note of both.
{self.name}'s herald read {parolee.name} their own parole, aloud, on {parolee.name}'s own quarterdeck.
{self.name} let {parolee.name}'s broken word go. It is a war, and words are the first thing it breaks.
{self.name} met {foe.name} of {foe.house} between the fleets and offered a white peace, and {foe.name} took it. The guns were never run out.
{self.name} and {foe.name} of {foe.house} met under a flag of truce and drank to each other's health, and went back to their ships to fight.
{self.name} met {foe.name} under a flag of truce and spent the hour counting {foe.house}'s ships. {foe.name} noticed, too late.
{self.name} sent {foe.name}'s herald back without an answer. The answer would come with the guns.
{self.name} bought from {sacker.house}'s plunder: metals and a crate of exotics, at half what the Exchange asks.
{self.name} put three hundred credits into {sacker.house}'s next raid beyond the rim, quietly, through a factor.
{self.name} rose in the Senate to ask why the houses that sack worlds beyond the rim pay nothing to the Reach that voted the war. {sacker.name} took it personally, which it was.
{self.name} bought nothing from {sacker.house}'s plunder and said nothing about it.
{self.name} kept the eight hundred credits that {partner.house}'s raids had made the house. The auditors' report named the house, and people read it.
{self.name} gave every credit the raids had made to the families of the crews who sailed on them. The auditors' report said so.
{self.name} kept five hundred credits from {partner.house}'s raids, and an auditor of the Senate kept the rest. The report did not mention the house.
{self.name} paid the house's crews off in full on the quay, six hundred credits, and the officers drank the house's health.
{self.name} gave the crews land on the house's worlds instead of coin. They will be there when the house needs them again.
{self.name} kept the crews under arms after the peace. The officers were glad of it; the towns they were quartered in were not.
{self.name} turned the crews loose at the peace without their pay. They went where unpaid crews go.
{self.name} laid a war tax on the people of the house's worlds. Six hundred credits came in, and a good deal of feeling.
{self.name} laid a levy on every cargo through the house's ports, for the war. The merchants paid five hundred credits, and remembered.
{self.name} sold the house's war stores on the Exchange, at the Exchange's price.
{self.name} asked nobody to pay for the war. The house would carry it, and so would {self.name}.
